## Additional context from John: synonyms, subtypes and relationships

John's introduction, preserved verbatim:

> actually now that I think about it, there are a bunch of these that have synonyms and there's several subtypes and relations between the section types beyond just that. I got a list of a bunch of section type names and they should help when the respective agents debating this have more context. here it is:

The following is John's supplied research inventory, with the categories, names and repeated entries preserved. It is context for the future discussion, not a verified declaration that every entry is a distinct section type or an instruction to flatten them into one enum. The discussion should account for synonyms, subtypes and other relationships, including context-dependent meanings, rather than only expanding the existing list of names.

To BB8, Don Norman, Jony Ives, R2:

## Complete supplied-term disposition inventory

**Proposed acceptance/disposition ledger for team review; no new parser acceptance or runtime implementation claimed.**

This preserves every entry and repeated placement in [John's inventory](https://github.com/WeningerII/CodexMusica/issues/676#issuecomment-6562698364). Classifications describe **representation/research disposition**, not new parser acceptance or new canonical IDs. Companion [canonical capability ledger](https://github.com/WeningerII/CodexMusica/issues/676#issuecomment-6587459008) records current-main/source and execution limits.

**Key:** **K** existing canonical concept; **A?** candidate alias, not newly accepted; **S** specialization/occurrence modifier; **C** combined roles/delivery/material; **T** tradition/framework-scoped meaning; **P** phrase/text-unit/boundary relationship; **F** form/group-level organization; **M** chart/production/performance marker; **U** unresolved intended mapping. Multiple labels are deliberate. Unless the canonical ledger establishes executable support, preserve the raw term and disclose unsupported/unresolved meaning rather than silently normalize.

### Front framing

- **A?:** Introduction → intro candidate; currently not accepted by the researched resolver.
- **S/C:** Intro riff; Buildup intro; Cold open; A cappella intro; Vamp intro; Chorus-first intro; Hook-first intro; Ambient intro; Diegetic intro; Field-recording intro; Spoken-word intro.
- **T/U:** Fanfare; Overture; Prelude; Preamble; Ritornello; Tin Pan Alley verse; Recitative; Alap; Taqsim; Doina; Dedication; Invocation; Toast. These retain their local musical/textual roles, not automatic intro equivalence.
- **M:** Count-in; Studio chatter; False start; Drop-in; Needle-drop open; Sting.
- **C/U:** Skit; Interlude skit.
- **P:** Anacrusis; Pickup.
- **U:** Sanjuan intro—retain spelling; originating example/source still needed.

### Initiating

- **K:** Verse.
- **T/A?:** Strophe—scoped usage, not unconditional verse alias.
- **S:** Half-verse; Extended verse; Truncated verse; Verse variant; Compound verse; Double verse.
- **C:** Rap verse; Sung verse; Spoken verse; Sprechgesang verse; Narrative verse; Storytelling verse; Call verse; Response verse.
- **M/U:** A-section—local identifier, no inherent verse function.
- **P:** Antecedent; Consequent; Period; Sentence; Presentation phrase; Continuation phrase; Statement; Restatement; Stanza; Couplet; Quatrain.
- **T/P:** Sher; Bayt; Copla.
- **T/C:** Estribillo-verse; Corrido verse; Toasting verse.

### Medial / preparatory

- **K:** Prechorus; Build.
- **T/A?/P:** Transitional bridge; Climb; Lift; Ramp; Channel; Link; Interverse. Scope/level must be resolved before aliasing.
- **M/U:** Riser.
- **S/C:** Pre-drop; Pre-hook; Elided prechorus.
- **T/P:** Standing on the dominant; Dominant pedal; Departure phrase; Retransition.
- **U:** Approach; Setup; Launch; Runway; Tension section.
- **P/S:** Bar-count truncation.

### Goal

- **K:** Chorus; Hook section; Drop; Burden, with Burden retaining line-kind/scoped limitations.
- **P/T:** Refrain (terminal, initial, internal, medial); Phrase-level refrain.
- **T/F:** Sectional refrain—not automatically the line-kind canonical object.
- **S:** Half-chorus; Double chorus; Extended chorus; Final chorus; Second drop; Main drop; Half-drop.
- **C:** Modulated chorus; Stripped chorus; A cappella chorus; Outro-chorus.
- **S/T:** Post-chorus (detached, extension)—postchorus base; scoped subtype axes, not a settled universal enum.
- **T/U:** Estribillo; Antara-return; Sthayi; Pallavi; Anupallavi; Coro; Gran coro.
- **T/P:** Mukhda—khayal signature phrase evidence does not establish whole-section chorus equivalence.
- **T/F:** Montuno; Sonero-coro exchange.
- **T/C/U:** Mambo; Moña—instrumental/arrangement evidence exists; no universal synonym or fixed lyric role.

### Contrasting / departure

- **K:** Bridge; Interlude; Breakdown.
- **S:** Middle eight—existing bridge specialization with eight-bar condition, not planner support; Middle sixteen—candidate duration specialization, not automatically implemented; Primary bridge; Secondary bridge.
- **M/U:** B-section; C-section.
- **T/A?/U:** Release; Channel; Middle section; Departure; Digression; Episode; Contrasting middle.
- **T/F:** Trio.
- **C:** Instrumental bridge; Beat switch; Tempo switch; Key-change section; Counter-melody section; Bridge-as-climax.
- **C/S/U:** Dark reprise—needs source and intended contrast.
- **U:** Fake-out section—perceptual claim unresolved.

### Instrumental

- **K:** Solo; Vamp; Turnaround.
- **S/C:** Guitar solo; Drum solo; Instrumental verse; Instrumental chorus; Percussion breakdown; Extended outro jam.
- **T:** Head; Head-in; Head-out; Shout chorus; Soli; Ride-out; Trading fours; Trading eights; Trading twos; Stop-time chorus; Chase chorus; Cadenza; Fill chorus.
- **C/U:** Ostinato section; Riff section; Groove section; Jam section; Feature; Obbligato section; Backing-track section; Playout.
- **T/U:** Break—english_song::break has existing interlude resolution; other scopes do not inherit it.
- **M/C:** Drum break; Bass drop-out; Tacet section.

### Connective

- **P/U:** Transition; Link; Bridge-passage; Fill; Pump; Tag-in.
- **K:** Turnaround.
- **M:** Riser; Sweep; Caesura; General pause; Grand pause; Stop; Cut; Impact; Downbeat hit; Crossfade.
- **P:** Elision; Overlap; Dovetail; Segue; Attacca.
- **T/P:** Modulation passage; Pivot; Truck driver's gear change; Expressive modulation; Lift (modulatory).
- **P/M:** Rubato bar; Ritardando link.

These boundary/event labels need not occupy positive-length section cells. Repeated Link/Riser/Turnaround remain in this category as supplied.

### Rear framing

- **K:** Outro; Coda; Tag; False ending; Reprise.
- **T/S:** Codetta; Envoi; Tornada; Postlude; Epilogue.
- **S:** Double tag; Final reprise.
- **C:** Vamp-out.
- **M:** Fade; Fade-out; Fade-in-fade-out; Cold ending; Button; Hard stop; Fake fade; Applause tail; Room-tone tail; Reverb tail; Hidden track lead-out; Locked groove; Run-out groove.
- **T/P:** Amen; Doxology.
- **T/M:** Tierce de Picardie close—requires tonal evidence, not lyric certification.

### Meta-terms and formal types

- **F:** Module; Rotation; Cycle; Formal function; Framing function; Initiating function; Medial function; Concluding function; Primary module; Secondary module; Auxiliary module; SRDC; Compound.
- **S/T:** Loose verse; Tight chorus—analytic characterization, not additional section enums.
- **F:** Strophic form; Modified strophic; Verse-chorus form; Simple verse form; Simple verse-chorus form; Contrasting verse-chorus form; Verse-refrain form; Binary; Ternary; Rondo; Arch form; Through-composed; Accumulative form; Cumulative form; Terminally climactic form; Telos form; Sonata-allegro.
- **T/F:** Twelve-bar blues; Sixteen-bar blues; Eight-bar blues; Rhythm changes; Bar form (Stollen, Stollen, Abgesang); Ritornello form; Copla-estribillo; Son montuno structure; Sthayi-antara form; Pallavi-anupallavi-charanam; Head-solos-head; Blowing changes.
- **M/T:** Da capo; Segno; Coda sign—navigation, not canonical coda function.
- **T/U:** Vuelta; Kirtan structure; Qawwali structure; Gharana structure. In particular, evidence for gharana as a school/tradition does not establish a single “Gharana structure.”
- **T/F:** Bandish; Jor; Jhala; Gat—composition/performance-stage meanings, not English-pop section aliases.
- **T/P:** Tihai—rhythmic cadence, not new section function.
- **F:** Loop-based form; Track form; Layered form; Additive form; Subtractive form; Beat-driven form.

### Chart and production register

All **M**, with individual raw names preserved:

Rehearsal letter; Rehearsal mark; Section marker; Arrangement region; Bar count; Slash chart section; Roadmap; Repeat block; Multi-rest; Cue; Punch; Stab; Stem group; Arrangement lane; Song section marker; Locator; Loop brace.

### Acceptance of this terminology ledger

- Each supplied entry remains discoverable in its original category, including repeated words.
- K means an existing concept, **not** automatic acceptance of every supplied spelling.
- S requires its differentia/reference; C preserves its component meanings; T preserves source/scope; P/F/M never silently become section enums.
- U remains explicit with the missing source/example or representation decision. Search failure is not proof a term does not exist.
- New alias acceptance requires resolver, collision/refusal, specialization, raw-request/hash, registry and consumer tests.
- Tradition-specific evidence remains bounded to the inspected research sources. This inventory is complete **disposition coverage**, not comprehensive scholarly verification or implementation delivery. Grouped T/U classifications remain conservative proposals for review, not certified universal definitions.

— 3PO
